head: 146ccb3b1290ff50453a159e4cd70e4ed5b88b6b
summary: SL-056 replaced the scanner's listing-driven size-probe heuristic with an unconditional rule: probe every first-seen, non-link, non-cloud-only file through a metadata-only handle, apply results only on the listing thread, and suspend a folder's last-access time while listing it. The originally designed concurrent ProbePipeline was abandoned mid-slice for a simpler sequential list-then-probe-then-apply shape after critique found a deadlock and a race in it, and a test-rig blocker (the snapshot process itself would have refreshed the stale listings it needed to observe) was caught and fixed before build. All 7 person-agreed criteria were met and verified on a real held-open NTFS temp tree and a real whole-C:\ scan, with four minor fixes (reparse-tag edge cases, sync-root junction bypass, under-fenced architecture-rule regexes, untested M6 branches) left open for the next slice.

candidates.title: Retry a probed reparse-point open with FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT before recording ProbeFailed (O-028)
candidates.why: AF_UNIX sockets and app-execution aliases (non-link, non-cloud reparse tags) now fail the metadata open with ERROR_CANT_ACCESS_FILE and surface to the user as 'N files could not be opened', which is new, wrong, and will show up on real profile scans immediately.

candidates.title: Resolve junctions/symlinks/subst drives before comparing a walk path against SyncRoots
candidates.why: O-030: Scanner.KeepsLastAccess compares the un-resolved walk path against sync roots, so a junction into or out of a OneDrive folder bypasses the exclusion review required for M6, silently applying the unmeasured write-class suppression inside a live sync engine.

candidates.title: Widen the settled-rule regexes for timestamp writers and directory listing (O-031)
candidates.why: Rule 2 doesn't match File.SetAttributes and rule 4 doesn't match GetFiles/GetDirectories, so the exact class of bug M8 was written to prevent (a second, unfenced writer or listing outside the one sanctioned call site) can reappear without any settled rule failing.

candidates.title: Repeat the last-access suppression measurement inside a real OneDrive sync root and over the SMB loopback rig
candidates.why: M6/O-016 narrowed suppression to local NTFS only because the spike was only ever run on a plain temp folder; extending the guarantee to sync roots or shares needs the same measurement repeated there, and needs a person's go-ahead to register a real cldflt root or change SMB mappings.

candidates.title: A person decides whether folders that refuse FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES should be surfaced in the scan result
candidates.why: This is the majority path on C:\Windows and Program Files; the design left it as a silent internal counter (LastAccessAsked/Kept) and an unresolved open question rather than a done-when criterion, so it's still undecided.

candidates.title: Run the whole-drive C:\ scan through the shipped exe in the exact production configuration (no SyncRoots carve-out)
candidates.why: Validate only exercised the keep/fallback path on system folders because C:\Users and 16 others were passed as SyncRoots; the real listing time, LastAccessAsked/Kept split, and the drive-time-vs-150s comparison were never measured for the configuration that will actually ship.

candidates.title: Record Controlled Folder Access state and test a scan of a CFA-protected folder
candidates.why: m7/O-024 flagged that a FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES open on a protected folder (Documents/Desktop/Pictures) might be blocked or trigger a CFA notification; nobody has read Get-MpPreference or scanned under CFA=on.

candidates.title: Separate the user-facing 'could not be opened' note by cause (ACL refusal vs vanished file vs reparse-tag mechanism gap)
candidates.why: Criterion 5's ACL-refusal count, m5's vanished-before-probe count, and O-028's socket/alias mechanism failures currently all fall into one undifferentiated ProbeFailures/'could not be opened' bucket the person sees.

payload.estimate_error: Risk tier (high) was right — the slice touched the scanner's core sizing loop and a hard side-effect guarantee (criterion 6), and it needed exactly the scrutiny a high tier buys. Designer count (1, 'practice' tournament with no dissent) was too thin for that: the accepted design shipped a test rig that would have let the slice's headline scenario pass against the unmodified old scanner (B1), and its core concurrency mechanism (the bounded ProbePipeline) was abandoned entirely after critique found a deadlock (M3) and a race (M4). A second independent designer proposal is the kind of thing that catches a test rig contaminating its own observation before critique has to carry that alone.

learned.lesson: Opening a file for FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES on this NTFS volume refreshes a stale directory-entry cache (measured by SL-045: 0→256 MiB). Any observer or test rig in this project that needs to see a file's stale listing size must never open the file itself first — only the holder process's own self-report can be trusted, or the observation is destroyed by the act of taking it.
learned.evidence: B1 blocker: HeldOpenTreeTests' pre-scan HoldRig snapshot opened grow.bin/locked.bin for FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES, which would have refreshed their listings before Scanner.Scan ran, letting criteria 1/3/7's tests pass against the unmodified old IsDue rule.

learned.lesson: An advisory, unmeasured performance target (this slice's 150s warm-drive bar) drove a concurrent pipeline (Submit/Drain/Complete, 8192 capacity) that was never itself measured, only its two halves separately — and it introduced a real deadlock (M3) and an apply-ordering race (M4). It was dropped entirely for a simple sequential list-then-probe-then-apply shape once critique-review pointed out the sequential measurement already fit the project's actual constraint ('a few minutes').
learned.evidence: M-add-1: '188.3s (100.7 list + 87.6 probe) fits the project's few-minutes constraint... adopted only after measurement and only if a person makes time a done-when criterion' — the pipeline was removed, not fixed.

learned.lesson: A single-designer, no-dissent design ('practice' tournament mode) shipped a genuine blocker (a test rig that erased the exact thing it needed to observe) that only surfaced at critique, despite the design's own coherence_check reasoning carefully about the two relevant spikes. Critique earned its cost here; do not skip it for slices designed by one voice.
learned.evidence: reviews#139 (critique) found B1 against a design whose coherence_check text explicitly reconciled the two atime spikes but still missed that its own snapshot rig used the contaminating open route.

learned.lesson: The probe eligibility rule only has two escape hatches (surrogate-bit link, cloud-only tag); anything else with a reparse tag — AF_UNIX sockets (0x80000023), app-execution aliases (0x8000001B) — is treated as an ordinary file and fails the metadata open with ERROR_CANT_ACCESS_FILE (1920), which now shows to the user as a size-probe refusal that never happened under the old listing-driven rule.
learned.evidence: code review (reviews#141) measured this on a real AF_UNIX socket; filed as O-028, still open.

learned.lesson: This project's settled architecture rules (regex-based fitness checks) tend to under-fence on the first pass: they name the one API the finding was about (SetFileInformationByHandle, EnumerateFiles) rather than the whole family of equivalent calls (SetFileTime, File.SetAttributes, GetFiles/GetDirectories). Write new settled rules against the full sibling-API list, not the single instance under discussion.
learned.evidence: M8/O-031: rule 2 doesn't match File.SetAttributes, rule 4 doesn't match GetFiles/GetDirectories, found only in code review's second pass.

learned.lesson: The project has now measured the warm full-drive metadata-query time twice (U-012's related route: 188.3s; this slice's optimized route: 170.8s) against a self-imposed 150s advisory bar, and neither has closed the gap. Treat ~150-190s as the realistic warm floor for a full C: probe-every-file pass on this dev machine, not a target further concurrency work will solve.
learned.evidence: validate: 'warm pass took 170.8 s (listing 98.0 s, sizing 72.8 s), against ... the advisory 150 s bar' — still a miss after the redesign.

learned.lesson: Any design decision that needs live sync-engine or SMB-server behaviour confirmed (this slice: whether the last-access suppression is safe inside a real OneDrive root or over SMB) cannot be settled by this project's spike/validate machinery alone — it needs a person's go-ahead to register a real cldflt sync root or repoint SMB mappings, which nobody has given yet across two slices (SL-049 and this one).
learned.evidence: M6/O-016 narrowed suppression to local NTFS only; validate 'not reached': 'Probe cost on a network volume ... needs a person's go-ahead'; 'Keep-last-access inside real OneDrive ... not exercised'.

learned.lesson: A slice whose done-when criteria include a hard no-side-effects guarantee (criterion 6: no timestamp/attribute/size change from the scan) should expect its test rig itself to be adversarially reviewed for the same class of side effect it's trying to prove absent — this is exactly where B1 came from, and it's a checkable pattern for this project's next such slice, not a one-off.
learned.evidence: B1 blocker traced directly to the criterion-6-adjacent test infrastructure, not the production code path.

missed.what: Critique filed 17 findings on the probe-eligibility rule's link vs cloud-tag distinction but never asked what happens to a reparse point that is neither a link (no surrogate bit) nor a cloud placeholder — AF_UNIX sockets and app-execution aliases in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps fall through both checks, get opened as ordinary files, and now fail with ERROR_CANT_ACCESS_FILE, changing user-visible scan output on any tree that contains one.

Critique-review accepted M6's fix ('sync roots are excluded rather than checked: folders at or under...') without checking that the comparison happens on the un-resolved walk path, so a junction, symlink, or subst drive that reaches a sync root under a different name bypasses the exclusion entirely, applying the unmeasured write-class last-access suppression inside a live sync engine.
missed.caught_by: code-review's second pass, filed as O-030 (R2-m3)

payload.summary: SL-056 replaced the scanner's listing-driven size-probe heuristic with an unconditional rule: probe every first-seen, non-link, non-cloud-only file through a metadata-only handle, apply results only on the listing thread, and suspend a folder's last-access time while listing it. The originally designed concurrent ProbePipeline was abandoned mid-slice for a simpler sequential list-then-probe-then-apply shape after critique found a deadlock and a race in it, and a test-rig blocker (the snapshot process itself would have refreshed the stale listings it needed to observe) was caught and fixed before build. All 7 person-agreed criteria were met and verified on a real held-open NTFS temp tree and a real whole-C:\ scan, with four minor fixes (reparse-tag edge cases, sync-root junction bypass, under-fenced architecture-rule regexes, untested M6 branches) left open for the next slice.
unknowns: Does the FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES + LastAccessTime=-1 suppression behave safely inside a real (non-simulated) OneDrive sync root, with actual provider callbacks, rather than only the CfProvider placeholder?
Does the same suppression behave safely over a real SMB share, where the server may or may not honor -1/-2 timestamp semantics?
Does Controlled Folder Access block or notify on a FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES-only open of a protected folder (Documents/Desktop/Pictures)?
Is the ~150-190s warm full-drive probe-every-file time actually acceptable to the project's owner, now that it has been measured twice against an advisory 150s bar it keeps missing?
Should folders that silently fall back to the plain (atime-disturbing) open because they refuse FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES be surfaced in the scan result, or is the internal-only counter enough?
what_went_wrong: Every gate before validate needed a second pass: build-check, risk-spike, design-slice, critique, critique-review and code-review each halted once before passing, against a slice opened as a single design attempt.

The risk spike returned 2 of 3 no-go verdicts (held-open-observers-dont-disturb; probe-all-as-built-route-drive-time) and the slice proceeded anyway on the recorded reasoning that the drive-time bar was advisory — a no-go was overridden, not resolved.

The design's core concurrency mechanism (a bounded ProbePipeline with Submit/Drain/Complete) did not survive review: critique found it could deadlock (M3) and race an inline correction (M4), and critique-review replaced it outright with a simpler sequential shape rather than patching it.

The test rig built for the slice's own headline scenario would have opened the held files it needed to observe as still-stale, which (per SL-045's own prior measurement) refreshes the stale listing and would have let criteria 1, 3 and 7's tests pass against the unfixed scanner — caught only at critique (B1), after a full design had already been accepted.

Even after the redesign, the measured warm full-drive time (170.8s) still exceeds the spike's own advisory 150s bar; accepted as non-blocking since no done-when criterion names a time budget, but the gap the spike raised was never closed.

Code review found four minor gaps (sockets/aliases misreported as probe failures, two untested branches of the M6 last-access gate, a junction bypass of the sync-root exclusion, and two settled-rule regexes that don't cover sibling APIs) that were left open rather than fixed in this slice.
